idiom_name: protected primitive API on a base class plus one abstract sandbox method per subclass
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: give the base class (a) a small set of protected operations, each hiding one interaction with the rest of the system and implemented once for every behaviour, and (b) one protected abstract entry point - the sandbox method, often the frame update - that every subclass implements and that nothing else overrides. Subclasses may use the provided operations and nothing else; state the rule and enforce it in review until the language can enforce it (protected, internal, pub(crate), module privacy), because the isolation is the point, not the inheritance. Keep the operations as high-level as the duplication demands: a primitive that only forwards to one call earns its place by hiding state or protecting an invariant, not by saving a line. When the base grows past a comfortable read, move clusters of primitives into collaborator objects reached through one protected accessor (getSoundPlayer()) instead of flattening them. Decide deliberately how the base receives the state its primitives need - constructor injection (explicit, but every derived constructor must forward it), factory-wrapped two-stage initialisation, static state (simple, but global), or a service locator (decoupled, but hidden dependencies) - and keep that state private.
code_sketch:
class Power:                                   # the base class
    def activate(self): raise NotImplementedError   # sandbox method: subclasses implement this
    # provided operations: the only route from a behaviour to the engine
    def play_sound(self, sound, volume=1.0): ...
    def spawn_particles(self, kind, count): ...

class SkyLaunch(Power):                        # a sandboxed subclass
    def activate(self):                        # composed from the primitives only
        self.play_sound(SOUND_SPROING)
        self.spawn_particles(PARTICLE_DUST, 10)
pitfalls: Subclasses that reach past the sandbox (importing the engine directly) restore the coupling the pattern removed and bypass its invariants; no type checker will report it.
A primitive set that only forwards to one engine call adds a layer without hiding anything or removing duplication.
Leaving the state-plumbing decision implicit produces half-initialised behaviours (two-stage init without a factory) or global mutable state that every subclass can poke at.

Subclasses overriding the provided operations - virtual by default in many languages - turns the sanctioned vocabulary into an extension point: the base's own code starts calling the overridden version and a later change to the primitive silently breaks whichever sibling depended on its real behaviour (the fragile base class problem from the subclass side); make primitives final/sealed wherever the language allows.

Assuming constructor pass-through works when the host creates the instances: engines and frameworks that instantiate subclasses themselves (Unity explicitly forbids MonoBehaviour constructors) make constructor injection impossible, so without a base-owned init hook that subclasses must not replace, the provided operations run against null subsystem references.
